abel_inverse — MATH transform op

• Data kinds: signal → signal

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.abel_inverse(A, dr: 'float' = 1.0, *, method: 'str' = 'derivative', n_quad: 'int' = 64) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import mathtransforms; mathtransforms.abel_inverse(A, dr: 'float' = 1.0, *, method: 'str' = 'derivative', n_quad: 'int' = 64) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsmath.get("abel_inverse"))

Usage

Recovers an axisymmetric distribution f(r) from the projection A(y) (inverse Abel transform = tomography of an axisymmetric object).

• "derivative" —— f(r) = −(1/π) ∫_r^R A'(y) / √(y² − r²) dy. Substituting y = √(r² + u²) removes the singularity, and A is differentiated with a cubic spline. Accurate for smooth projections, but differentiation amplifies noise:

the noise error grows inversely with the sample spacing dr (measured 2026-10-03, 1% noise: 80 → 640 samples gives

mean error 0.027 → 0.237, log-log slope ≈ 1). On coarse grids this one is better.

• "onion" —— onion peeling: f is taken as constant per shell of radius dr, and the upper-triangular matrix of chord lengths is solved from the outside in. Resolution is set by the shell width; since no derivative is taken, noise grows more slowly (same measurement: 0.036 → 0.100, slope ≈ 1/2). In measurements on fine grids, this one wins (1/2.4 of the derivative's error at n=640); on coarse grids (n≈80) it reverses.

The 2 are independent discretizations, so applying both to the same projection and checking the discrepancy serves as a cross-check.

Gate: from A(y) = √π σ exp(−y²/σ²), f(r) = exp(−r²/σ²).

Family-wide input contract (fail-closed)

Every mathops op validates its input before computing (nothing slips through silently):

• complex input raises ValueError — coercing to float64 silently discards the imaginary part (numpy only emits a ComplexWarning and returns a plausible-looking wrong real number). State .real/.imag/abs() explicitly, or use complexops, which handles complex data.

• masked arrays with masked elements raise ValueError — the implicit conversion that peels off the mask and uses the raw values underneath is refused. Say explicitly whether to fill or to drop.

• NaN/Inf raises ValueError on every input (refused with the count stated — it propagates through the whole result).

• Shapes are strict: 1-D and 2-D are never implicitly promoted or broadcast (a matrix in a vector slot, or a vector in a matrix slot, raises ValueError; reshape explicitly).

• Size cap: ops that take a matrix, and the stat_histogram bins, raise ValueError beyond mathops.MAX_ELEMENTS (2^26 ≈ 67 million elements).
